assessment: Gishath costs {5}{R}{G}{W}, exactly two cards in the 99 make a command-zone cast cheaper, and goldfish puts his mean cast at turn 7.969. So four of these ten buy ignition, three buy colour, two widen the enrage web's damage class, and one is pure ceiling. The enrage web is the second engine and it is one free repeatable damage source deep — Forerunner of the Empire, a 1/3 — so three picks widen that class instead of adding another body that waits to be hurt. Nothing here moves the computed bracket floor: it is already 4, on a Polyraptor + Forerunner of the Empire infinite tag that stack 003 resolved as bounded at seven tokens.

combo_lines_opened.produces: a mandatory loop neither player can stop from inside — a drawn game unless the deck supplies its own loop-breaker

ten.closes: engine component: fodder — the free repeatable self-ping
ten.why: Two mana that answers both named single points of failure at once: 'Creature spells you cast cost {1} less to cast' reaches the command zone, and 'Whenever another creature you control enters, this creature deals 2 damage to it' is a second free repeatable ping beside Forerunner of the Empire — so a turn-7 Gishath connection that drops four Dinosaurs pings all four and fires Ripjaw Raptor, Ranging Raptors, Trapjaw Tyrant and Polyraptor in the same event, with no combat step needed for plan B.
ten.unlocks: Plan A feeding plan B: the reveal event becomes the damage event. The price is stated in stack 002 and is not small — Polyraptor resolving under it is a drawn game with no outlet on board, and the 2-damage ping kills Otepec Huntmaster (1/2) and Intrepid Paleontologist (2/2) on the way in, though Forerunner (1/3) survives.

ten.closes: engine component: ignition — making Gishath castable
ten.why: Colourless, so it pays nothing into a mana base already 16 sources short in white and red, and it does two jobs: 'Creature spells you cast of the chosen type cost {1} less to cast' takes {1} off the command-zone cast every time including the tax on recast, and the upkeep look-at-top converts a dead draw step into a Dinosaur about three times in ten off 29 Dinosaur copies in 99.
ten.unlocks: Turn-3 Horn into turn-6 Gishath off seven lands rather than eight, and a free card-selection trickle for the turns you spend ramping.

count the ramp itself as curve

ten.closes: engine component: ignition — making Gishath castable
ten.why: 'Dinosaur spells you cast cost {2} less to cast' is the largest single discount available to this commander, matching Urza's Incubator at half the setup, and it discounts 29 other Dinosaurs on the same axis the ramp count is already paying for.
ten.unlocks: The three-reducer board — Otepec Huntmaster, Urza's Incubator and this — where Gishath costs {1}{R}{G}{W} — four mana, against a goldfish mean available mana of 4.895 at turn 5. The honest cost is that a Human Knight is not revealed by the trigger, not discounted by Incubator, and not shielded by Temple Altisaur.

ten.why: Naming Dinosaur gives an untapped source of any colour for Gishath and for 29 of the 34 creature copies, which is the exact shape of a shortfall that is 16 sources deep in white and red and not in total mana, and 'that spell can't be countered' protects the one cast the whole deck is built around against the blue seat.
ten.unlocks: An untapped triple-pip fixer that Secluded Courtyard and Unclaimed Territory only half provide, and a Gishath cast that a held counterspell cannot punish.

ten.why: Two mana for a damage source that costs no mana per use and can point at your own board: 'Sacrifice a creature: This enchantment deals 1 damage to any target' arms Ripjaw Raptor, Ranging Raptors, Trapjaw Tyrant, Wrathful Raptors and Polyraptor at instant speed, and the fodder is free once Polyraptor is making copies.

Whether the three-card board is a kill rather than a longer loop needs /resolve-stack.

ten.why: '{T}: Add one mana of any color' for {G} on turn one adds a source to white and to red — the two colours sitting at 20 against a Karsten yardstick of 36 — and pulls the whole eight-mana clock forward a turn, which is the only thing that reliably beats the turn-8 median cast.
ten.unlocks: Turn-2 three-mana plays and a white source for Austere Command and Trapjaw Tyrant off a deck that fails to make WW about as often as it makes it. Note that a 0/1 dies to Marauding Raptor's ping if both are sleeved, and that this takes land copies from 35 to 34.

citations.quote: Read them as a budget, not a table

ten.why: The obsolescence index lists Farseek as a replacement for Kodama's Reach, and in this 99 the reason is colour rather than cost: 'Search your library for a Plains, Island, Swamp, or Mountain card' fetches Jetmir's Garden, Canopy Vista or Cinder Glade, so it is one of the few ramp spells that answers white or red instead of the green the deck already has 26 sources of.
ten.unlocks: A turn-2 accelerant that also fixes the worst colour, and a turn-3 four-mana play toward the commander instead of a turn-3 Kodama's Reach that ends on the same three lands in play.

citations.quote: triple pips and three colours do not coexist

ten.why: Imprint any creature card and 'Spells you cast that share a card type with the exiled card cost {2} less to cast' applies to Gishath and to all 34 creature copies — the {2} that Knight of the Stampede gives, colourless, and reaching the six entries at mana value 8 or more that the curve reading names as the liability.
ten.unlocks: Taken with the three reducers ranked above it, a cost-reduction class the diagnosis sizes at two becomes six — past the five copies the redundancy citation prices at 31% of openers. The price is a card from hand at imprint and a fizzle if the Anvil eats artifact removal before the payoff.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite death triggers, Infinite ETB, Infinite LTB

ten.closes: engine component: fodder — the free repeatable self-ping
ten.why: 'Whenever another creature you control enters, this creature deals damage equal to that creature's power to any target' turns the stack-001 reveal — four Dinosaurs entering at once — into about twenty damage aimed wherever you like, including at your own Ripjaw Raptor or Polyraptor to open the enrage web without attacking.
ten.unlocks: A free repeatable damage source that scales with the bodies the commander is already producing, and a second use for every Dinosaur cast from hand. Off-tribe, so the reveal skips it, Urza's Incubator will not discount it, and Temple Altisaur will not shield it.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite combat phases, Infinite colored mana, Infinite untap of creatures you control

ten.why: The one pick here that closes nothing the diagnosis measured, and it is on the list because Selvala, Heart of the Wilds is already in the 99: she taps for mana equal to the greatest power among your creatures, so with a 7-power Gishath on board the {3}{R}{R} untap is mana-positive, and each extra combat is another Gishath reveal.
ten.unlocks: A second and third connection on the turn you finally cast him — the difference between one reveal of seven and a board that empties the library's Dinosaurs. The line is unverified: whether Selvala's X actually exceeds five reliably, and whether the loop terminates on your terms, needs a stack scenario.

citations.quote:
each return trip to the command zone adds {2} per
prior command-zone cast (Miljkovac)

gaps: No synergy-partner claim is made anywhere above, deliberately. The synergy graph returns the same five in-deck partners — Sol Ring, Command Tower, Arcane Signet, Exotic Orchard, Path of Ancestry — for Marauding Raptor, Herald's Horn, Knight of the Stampede, Kinjalli's Caller, Goblin Anarchomancer and all three Medallions, on a format-wide 'Ramp + Cost Reduction' rule. It locates cost reducers; it cannot rank them for this deck.

The obsolescence index also lists Farseek, Three Visits and Nature's Lore as replacements for Skyshroud Claim. That entry is a mana-value artifact and is not used above: Skyshroud Claim puts TWO Forest cards onto the battlefield untapped, which none of the three do.

Three Visits carries the same index hit against Kodama's Reach that Farseek does and is not on the list, because it searches a Forest card — green is the colour with 26 sources, and the shortfall is white and red at 20 each.

Aether Flash is the other free repeatable self-ping in the pool and is not on the list: the combo database gives it the same 'Draw the game' tag with Polyraptor that stack 002 verified for Marauding Raptor, and unlike Marauding Raptor it buys no cost reduction back. Chandra's Ignition and Star of Extinction are off for the opposite reason — one-shots that sweep the converters they are meant to arm.

Whether Gishath's simultaneous put-onto-the-battlefield event gives Marauding Raptor or Terror of the Peaks a trigger per Dinosaur, and whether enrage bodies entering in that same event get pinged, is unresolved — /resolve-stack would settle it. The ignition case for Marauding Raptor does not rest on it; the fodder case partly does.

Whether Marauding Raptor plus Goblin Bombardment converts stack 002's drawn game into a kill, and whether Aggravated Assault plus Selvala terminates on your terms, are both unverified. Two scenarios, one rules domain each.
There is no deck_recon.json for this deck, so nothing above is measured against what strong Gishath lists actually run — every pick is derived from this deck's own audit figures and oracle text.

No goldfish target prices a conjunction, so no measured rate says how often a converter body and a damage source arrive together. The three fodder picks are sized off the single-card class the diagnosis names, not off a simulated rate.
